Each find is said three times, a cell each: the bass alone, then with the ring remembering, then with the ring caught up. The tune is four notes, and so is a line of four words. Now the middle cell of each three is SUNG, on the notes found so far, each note its own word; and because the notes come back last first, so do the words: 'was' (1:36.7); 'it was' (1:43.1); 'where it was' (1:49.2); 'right where it was' (1:55.4-1:57.8). The song says its own name once, in the cell after the tune is whole again, and at 2:00 the band is back.
THE BASS AND THE RING REST WHILE IT IS SUNG, and that was not the plan: it is what the words needed. Sung over the bass as written, the recogniser (small.en, each phrase cut from the mix) read 3 of the 10 words, and never more than 4 with the voice 6 dB hotter, brighter, an octave up, or sung early: with the voice and the fretless alone it read 0 of 10; with the voice and the ring and glass, or the voice and the toms, 9 of 10. (A floor-tom stroke under the last word was rested in between and is back: with the ring out it makes no difference, 9 of 10 either way on all three seeds.) So each find now has three speakers in turn: THE BASS FINDS IT, THE VOICE NAMES IT, THE BASS AND THE RING KEEP IT. Under the voice there is only the toms' bar time and the held glass. Ten fretless notes and six ring notes are left out; no other note changes.
